sections.Assignment Description:
On Thursday of the 7th instructional week, students will take a midterm exam devoted to the
socio-historical contexts in which the Eastern European Jewish literature covered in class arose
and theoretical concepts related to it. The test will have a closed-ended, quiz format. All the
questions will refer directly to the topics covered in class, 20 questions.

categories.name: Midterm Oral Exam

assignments.name: Midterm Oral Exam — instructional week 8 (15-min quote presentation, 60 pts max)

sections.Assignment Description:
During the 8th instructional week, each student will deliver a 15-minute oral presentation on a
quote from any of the readings covered so far. The presentation has to cover: 1. A thesis: what do
you want to prove by selecting the quote? 2. Formal literary devices, in the context of the thesis.
3. Role of the quote in the larger context of a book. 4. Historical/Philosophical background of the
quote. After the presentation, 5. the instructor will ask challenging follow-up questions about the
quote and the book as a whole, and the student has to prepare to defend their position and
interpretation. 6. The presentation has to be delivered according to the high standards of public
speaking: no repetitions, confident voice, no filler words, appropriate cadence and rhythm. 10
points available for satisfying each item. 60-points maximum.

assignments.name: Final Oral Exam — last instructional week (15-min presentation on Love/Tradition/Jewishness/Violence/Humor across 3 read

sections.Assignment Description:
During the last instructional week, each student will deliver a 15-minute oral presentation on a
topic of: 1. Love, 2. Tradition, 3. Jewishness, 4. Violence, 5. Humor as reflected in three
self-selected readings covered in the class. The student has to thoroughly explain 1. how the
readings address the problem, both formally and content-wise (specific examples), 2. what
differences and similarities there are between them, 3. What general conclusion can be drawn

-- 3 of 11 --

from said comparison, and how do the readings shine a new light on the theoretical problem?
After the presentation, 4. the instructor will ask challenging follow-up questions, and the student
has to prepare to defend their position and interpretation. 5. The presentation has to be delivered
according to the high standards of public speaking: no repetitions, confident voice, no filler
words, appropriate cadence and rhythm. 10 points available for satisfying each item. 50 points
maximum.
